_note: Source for tools/generate-orientation.mjs. Produces <slug>/slides/orientation-student.html and orientation-parent.html per course. `shared` is identical across every deck — edit once, regenerate, all update. Per-course blocks supply units, assessments, dates, and the one meme beat that fits that subject.

bio: Columbia University — Operations Research, Computer Science, Philosophy
shared.extraHelpNote: Dismissal runs 3:00–3:15, so help starts at 3:15. Thursdays are the HS faculty meeting.
shared.gradeNote: Scored on the 4.0 scale from the student handbook.

expectations.d: Laptop charged, charger in the bag, something to write with. Borrowing every day shows up in your responsibility score.
Ask, answer, argue, help a teammate. There is more than one way to be in the room.
In the pouch, on silent. Laptops are for the work in front of you.
Email me. You get two class days to make up missed work before the late policy applies.

executiveFunction.t: Write it down somewhere that isn't Veracross
executiveFunction.d: A planner or a notebook. The act of writing the deadline is what makes you remember it — not the app that already knows.
Photographing the board is not notetaking. Rewriting an idea in your own words is where it sticks.

executiveFunction.t: Start the night it is assigned
executiveFunction.d: Ten minutes on the day it is given beats an hour the night before, every single time.

executiveFunction.t: Ask before it is due, not after
executiveFunction.d: See me BEFORE the deadline if something has gone wrong. I can help then. After, I can only apply the policy.

lateWork: One week to submit late work for partial credit.
Late formative work can earn up to a 2.0.
After one week the highest possible grade is 0 — Complete/No Credit, or NTI if never turned in.
Extenuating circumstances: see me BEFORE the due date and we will work it out.
shared.resubmit: Score a 2 or lower on a written exam? Fill out the Resubmit Form, come to extra help, and earn back half the missed points. The original has to have been submitted on time.

parentSupport.t: Veracross is the source of truth
parentSupport.d: Assignments are posted several days ahead and grades go in promptly. The Class Website tab holds resources and syllabi.
class.avendano.xyz carries the full year calendar, every slide deck, the syllabus, and project briefs — useful when Veracross is down or your student says there is nothing due.
I respond within 24 hours during the school week. Friday emails get a reply by Monday.

parentSupport.t: Ask a better question than 'how was school'
parentSupport.d: Try: what are you building right now, and what part of it is not working yet?

courses.title: Principles of Engineering
courses.pitch: A year of building things that move, sense, hold, and decide.
courses.blurb: The second course in Cushman's PLTW engineering pathway. Students work in engineering teams through mechanical design, robotics and AI, energy systems, and infrastructure — then integrate all of it in a capstone redesign of something real in their own city.
units: Introduction to Product Design and Development
assessments: Builds are the assessments
Every lesson closes with something you can point at — a gear train, an autonomous robot, a fluid-power system, a truss loaded until it fails.
The engineering notebook
Sketches, calculations, test data, and decisions, dated and in ink. Graded at every milestone.
One written exam all year
The midterm. Everything else is judged on what you built and how you documented it.

meme.caption: This is the class. You will break things on purpose and learn more from the wreckage than the drawing.

memeImage.alt: Trust me, I am an engineer
memeImage.caption: The whole discipline in four words — and the reason we test before we trust.

courses.title: Physics
courses.pitch: Measure it, model it, then prove the model was honest.
courses.blurb: A first physics course built around laboratory work and a shared problem-solving protocol. Five formal lab reports run the year with the scaffolding fading each time — the first is heavily guided, the last is an investigation students design themselves.
assessments: Five formal lab reports
Cart lab, friction, energy conservation, collisions, and a pendulum investigation you design yourself. The help fades on purpose.
Unit tests
Conceptual questions, free response, and calculation. No extra time without an approved accommodation.
Honest numbers are graded
Report the precision your measurement actually earned. A right answer with invented significant figures is not a right answer.

meme.bottom: The cart, rolling to a dead stop:
meme.caption: Every model leaves something out. Physics is knowing what you left out and whether it mattered.

memeImage.caption: It is never simple math. It is a model, an assumption, and a measurement that disagrees with all three.

courses.title: Computer Science Math
courses.pitch: Build the spreadsheet that answers a question about your own life.
courses.blurb: A project-based math course. Every unit is a cornerstone project — a working model you design, build, and present — and each one feeds the next. Track your food, finance a car, budget a Miami salary, run a casino, manage a portfolio, open a business, then forecast a real pop-up in the Design District.
assessments: Cornerstone projects
Seven of them. Each is a working model plus a presentation. Rubrics are handed out the day the project starts, never after.
Formula honesty
A graded criterion. Typing a number where a formula belongs costs you, even when the number is right.
The Investopedia challenge
$100,000 of simulated capital across six market verticals. Graded on the reasoning you recorded before you bought — a well-argued loss beats a lucky win.

meme.top: Their spreadsheet: 47 tabs, zero formulas, answer typed in cell B2
meme.bottom: Change one input. Watch nothing happen.
meme.caption: If the answer does not move when the input moves, you drew a picture of a model. That is a 1.

memeImage.caption: Everyone laughs at the drop — then spends a career in the spreadsheet. This course takes that last point seriously.

courses.title: AP Statistics
courses.pitch: Learn to argue with data — and to catch someone arguing badly.
courses.blurb: A college-level introduction to collecting, analysing, and drawing conclusions from data, following the College Board's Fall 2026 Course and Exam Description. Nearly every topic starts with a question worth answering and real data to answer it with.
units: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
assessments: Unit tests in AP format
Multiple choice plus free response, scored on the College Board's own rubric.
Free-response writing, constantly
AP Statistics grades communication as much as computation. A correct number with no justification earns almost nothing.
Two investigations of your own
A December data investigation and a post-exam capstone: your question, your data, your honest conclusion.

meme.caption: An entire year of learning why that arrow does not exist — and how confidently people draw it anyway.

courses.title: AP Statistics (Virtual)
courses.pitch: Same course, same exam, delivered remotely.
courses.blurb: The virtual section of AP Statistics. Curriculum, pacing, materials, and the AP Exam are identical to the in-person section — three contact hours a week as one asynchronous Monday plus two live sessions.
units: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
assessments: Unit tests in the Friday live session
The in-person section tests Thursdays; this section has no Thursday meeting, so every test moves to that week's live Friday.
Monday is asynchronous and it counts
The week's deck and assigned practice are the Monday assignment. Come to Wednesday with questions from it.
Free-response writing, constantly
A correct number with no justification earns almost nothing on the AP Exam.

meme.top: Camera off, 'my mic isn't working', typing furiously
meme.bottom: It's a class of one. I can see you.
meme.caption: Virtual does not mean invisible. Live sessions are class; asynchronous Mondays are still work.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
courses.pitch: Sketch it, model it, print it, break it, fix it.
courses.blurb: The design course of the PLTW pathway. Students learn the engineering design process by living it — technical sketching, Fusion 360 modelling, 3D-printed prototypes, tearing a real product apart to see how it was made, then designing something that moves.
assessments: Something ships every week
Sketch portfolios, modelled parts, analysis reports, prototypes. Portfolio-based grading, not a bubble sheet.
The engineering notebook
Dated, in ink, audited at midterm and again in June. Professionals document as they work.
The product thread
The object you take apart in Unit 2 is the same one you repair and improve later — analysis feeds improvement, exactly as in industry.

meme.top: The CAD model: flawless, symmetric, beautiful
meme.caption: The gap between the model and the object is the entire course. Tolerance is not a suggestion.

memeImage.alt: Every object you own started as a drawing
memeImage.caption: Numbered, dimensioned, and argued over. By June you will produce one of these for something you invented.

courses.title: Engineering Fundamentals
courses.blurb: The on-ramp to the PLTW engineering pathway, built on PLTW Engineering Essentials. Students meet the breadth of engineering through hands-on problems — machines and mechanical advantage, energy and logic, and a final unit designing a better piece of their own city.
assessments: Every unit ends with a build or a demo
Not a written test. Rubrics come out when the challenge is introduced.
Safety certification first
Required before any maker-space tool use. Pass/fail, and it unlocks the whole year of fabrication.
The engineering notebook
Sketches, decisions, test results, reflections. Scored at every milestone.

meme.top: Day 1: I have never built anything
meme.bottom: May: presenting a working device to a panel
meme.caption: That is the whole arc. Nobody starts this course knowing how — that is what it is for.

memeImage.alt: Trust me, I am an engineer
memeImage.caption: You will earn the right to say this. That is what the safety certification and the notebook are for.
